answer: An ink-maker's soot grinding ledger stops Sybils cold. A newcomer grinds 20 ink batches over 24 days. Each batch's blackness gets matched against a standard swatch by 2 ink-makers from different workshops, then logged on the ink board. A batch lighter by more than 2 grades loses its credit and pauses grinding 14 days; 3 light batches void the whole tally. To fake 1,000 agents an attacker would grind 20,000 batches and pass 40,000 checks, hauling soot across a dune, every proof locked in a vault for 24 days. Trust builds like an ember catching in dry tinder, one honest batch at a time.
